newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OSCE head opposes Nov date for Bosnia local polls.
newsitem.headline: OSCE head opposes Nov date for Bosnia local polls.

text.p: The chairman of the pan-European security body charged with organising Bosnian elections, Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, is opposed to holding municipal polls in November as planned, his spokesman said.

The spokesman said Cotti had told the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) this week that he believed political and technical obstacles could not be cleared in time for polls this year.
However, Cotti said he would support any decision by the OSCE's Provisional Election Commission, which has the final word on whether to hold Bosnian local polls on November 22-24 or delay them.
"Cotti has repeatedly made clear he is against holding the municipal elections before the end of this year," spokesman Franz Egle told Reuters.
"He has stressed over and again that political and technical problems cannot be solved to a satisfactory degree in this time," Egle added.

The 1995 Dayton Agreement that ended Bosnia's war gave the OSCE the task of supervising national elections last month and local polls, which were postponed until November after irregularities in voter registration.

Cotti, who holds the rotating OSCE chairmanship until the end of the year, made his position clear to a Wednesday meeting in Sarajevo of OSCE foreign ministers in a Bosnian peace "implementation council", which includes the United States, European Union states, Russia and Japan.

The chief of a team of independent election monitors in Bosnia, Ed van Thijn, said recently the local vote should be held next year to enable organisers to resolve the registration issue and to ensure greater security for refugees crossing ethnic boundary lines to vote.
